question: What should the next Composer campaign look like?
context: The orange-and-white mark is already approved. These three directions use it unchanged. Each gives a first-time visitor a different reason to pay attention.
target: Choose the clearest high-character campaign for indie makers. Judge the actual posters in order: Press Run, Signal Test, App Parts. Weigh authorship and memorable art alongside the product promise.

options.title: Press Run
options.pitch: An orange workshop poster with the real Composer press as the single subject.
options.outcome: Visitors associate Composer with making and operating something they own.
options.pro: Distinctive campaign artwork and a clear, direct promise.
options.con: The machine needs a product example beside it on the landing page.

options.title: Signal Test
options.pitch: An ink-and-electric-cyan field report with LoftwahFM’s Low Tide cover from the published 30-second Studio film.
options.outcome: A finished piece earns the click and leads into how it was made.
options.pro: Shows the calibre of published work and gives the campaign an editorial voice.
options.con: Film-led imagery can make Composer look like Studio unless the story names the connection.

options.title: App Parts
options.pitch: A white, orange and acid-yellow parts diagram. Three real jobs form the product story.
options.outcome: A new visitor understands the mechanics before taking a first step.
options.pro: Strong silhouette at small size and a system that can extend to documentation.
options.con: An art-led release can feel more expressive than a product diagram.

question: What should the Composer homepage show first?
context: The homepage needs to bring newcomers into an actual first success while giving the brand a recognisable opening.
target: For a new indie builder, prioritise understanding the product and finding a useful first action. Consider the art-removal regression.

options.title: A live app with its build path
options.pitch: Feature one working app, its source and a direct route to build something like it.
options.outcome: Newcomers can connect the promise to a real result and see what to do first.
options.pro: Shows ownership and use in the same opening.
options.con: Needs a strong maintained example with reproducible instructions.

options.title: Workshop art paired with a live handoff
options.pitch: Keep one large authored scene beside the actual first-app action and a linked result.
options.outcome: The opening has more character while the first action stays visible.
options.pro: Gives Composer an immediately recognisable visual world.
options.con: The art competes for space on small screens.

options.title: Choose a job first
options.pitch: Lead with Build an app, Connect an existing app and Find a resource.
options.outcome: People with a specific goal can go straight to the matching workflow.
options.pro: Fast to scan and easy to maintain.
options.con: The opening has less room to show why Composer feels different.

question: How should Share help you find something worth using?
context: The catalogue can open with artwork and still make finding relevant, reusable work easy. Saved feedback is available when signed in.
target: Pick the best starting point for reaching one useful item and understanding reuse. Consider both deliberate lookup and browsing.

options.title: Three useful collections
options.pitch: Lead with a print, an editable asset and a palette. Each opens a working resource with credit and reuse details.
options.outcome: People who are browsing find distinct useful objects sooner.
options.pro: Gives the artwork an editorial reason to be featured.
options.con: Picks need upkeep and rights review.

options.title: Search with reuse filters
options.pitch: Lead with search and project, rights and file-type filters. Show matched artwork immediately.
options.outcome: Visitors with a particular need spend less time opening irrelevant work.
options.pro: Scales to a large collection.
options.con: A person browsing for inspiration may have no good query.

options.title: Follow a collection from one strong piece
options.pitch: Feature a relevant original, then let visitors follow its project and related formats.
options.outcome: Readers understand one object in depth and get useful discovery paths from it.
options.pro: Feeds curiosity with a real creative story.
options.con: A weak lead makes the whole entry feel irrelevant.

question: Which feedback controls should be easiest to reach?
context: A signed-in owner needs to react when the problem is evident, including weak features and hard-to-find resources.
target: Choose the feedback affordance that captures the most actionable evidence with the least distraction. Evaluate options individually. The owner can choose multiple.

options.title: On the item
options.pitch: Give each artwork detail a private action for featuring, hiding or explaining an issue.
options.outcome: Feedback carries the exact artwork context.
options.pro: Easy to act at the moment of judgement.
options.con: Does little for the problem of never finding an item.

options.title: On search results
options.pitch: Offer a quick note when a query disappoints, with an explicit choice to include that query.
options.outcome: Search misses become directly diagnosable.
options.pro: Captures failed discovery before a visitor leaves.
options.con: The prompt needs careful placement to keep results readable.

options.title: In a private shortlist
options.pitch: Compare saved pieces and record why one earns a place over another.
options.outcome: Useful reasoning travels with creative selections.
options.pro: Supports considered editorial work in batches.
options.con: Adds a step when the owner wants immediate feedback.

question: What should Studio feature as proof of its work?
context: A striking frame can invite interest. A visible process and a finished result tell creators what Studio can do for them.
target: Choose the strongest honest proof for a visitor deciding whether to try Studio. Check that the evidence gives Studio a distinctive voice.

options.title: A finished cut with its edit
options.pitch: Use the published 30-second Studio film, which opens on LoftwahFM’s Low Tide cover. Put a strong final frame beside the edit and link directly to playback.
options.outcome: Visitors can see the finished work and understand how the shot became a cut.
options.pro: Turns artwork into credible workflow proof.
options.con: A film-forward story can underrepresent image and audio work.

options.title: Three finished formats
options.pitch: Show one strong finished still, one video frame and one audio release, each with its source when available.
options.outcome: Visitors can identify the format they want to make.
options.pro: Shows breadth and puts genuinely different work in view.
options.con: Three pieces compete for the same headline.

options.title: A playable sample project
options.pitch: Offer one guided sample edit with its published export and a direct editing entry.
options.outcome: Visitors experience the tool before making an account commitment where access permits.
options.pro: Demonstrates utility by doing.
options.con: Needs a safe maintained demo and a clear recovery path.

question: How much character should Paperwork put around signing?
context: The paper press gives the product a recognisable opening. Signing and legitimate document handling remain the priority.
target: For a person who has a PDF ready, balance an immediate clear action, perceived trust and distinctiveness. Avoid relying on actual personal documents.

options.title: Paper press beside the drop zone
options.pitch: Put the authored press in a bounded visual panel and keep the signing action visible at phone size.
options.outcome: Visitors get a recognisable product without hunting for the PDF action.
options.pro: Recovers character while keeping the task obvious.
options.con: On small screens the press may need a tighter, purpose-made crop.

options.title: Let the sample do the talking
options.pitch: Show a clean white sample document with a visible place to sign and a clear try-it action.
options.outcome: People understand the workflow before using their own document.
options.pro: The visual demonstrates the actual job.
options.con: A document preview needs strong art direction to earn attention.

options.title: Straight to signing
options.pitch: Lead with drop or choose PDF. Use the press as the campaign and editorial signature.
options.outcome: Repeat signers reach the tool with the least friction.
options.pro: Protects clarity when the job is urgent.
options.con: Gives the public opening less identity.

question: Where should Spin put its energy?
context: The wheel is both the action and the signature. The current direction needs stronger character without making the controls harder to find.
target: Recommend a visibly lively opening that lets a new visitor add choices and spin within seconds. Treat the prior Clef tie as unresolved evidence.

options.title: Make the live wheel the show
options.pitch: Give the functioning wheel the largest space, with saturated wedges, clear inputs and a deliberate result reveal.
options.outcome: A visitor learns Spin by doing the one memorable action.
options.pro: The expressive element is the actual product.
options.con: The layout and motion need restraint around accessibility and long lists.

options.title: Give it a host
options.pitch: Put an original game-show host in presets and result states beside a clean wheel.
options.outcome: Repeat use gains a distinctive voice and surprise.
options.pro: Character can change by context without moving the controls.
options.con: Requires excellent original character work and carries higher taste risk.

options.title: Run it like a party tool
options.pitch: Lead with event-ready wheel presets, easy editing and a large audience view.
options.outcome: Hosts move faster from idea to a usable live game.
options.pro: Gives Spin a clear audience and purpose.
options.con: A party-first presentation can feel excessive for everyday decisions.

question: What belongs in the next set of public shareables?
context: The first image needs to earn its placement. A useful object, a real result or a specific announcement gives it something to say.
target: For earning a meaningful click from builders or creators in a feed, rank each format. Prefer a concrete link destination and avoid judging by polish alone.

options.title: An original people can use
options.pitch: Feature one usable resource, its creator and the exact destination. Compose for a readable feed crop.
options.outcome: People can see the value and reach the item in one step.
options.pro: The card can show the actual asset at a meaningful size.
options.con: Needs reliable rights, credits and a useful destination.

options.title: Show what changed
options.pitch: Use one frame pair, real product detail or concrete before-and-after for a meaningful release.
options.outcome: People can understand the improvement without reading a long post.
options.pro: Makes a product claim easy to verify.
options.con: Weak changes and cluttered screenshots produce weak cards.

options.title: One event or invitation
options.pitch: Use committed brand colour, a crisp headline and only the details a reader needs to act.
options.outcome: The announcement is identifiable and useful at small sizes.
options.pro: Strong composition with very little material.
options.con: Needs a real occasion or the card will feel generic.

question: What should make someone want to try Prints?
context: Prints Desktop can compare actual cuts and keep work attached to its source. The published walkthrough is an existing piece of proof.
target: Pick the best entry for an unfamiliar creator to understand why Prints is worth installing. Keep platforms and proof accurate.

options.title: Compare things you almost kept
options.pitch: Lead with real alternate cuts and the decision that selected the original.
options.outcome: Creators recognise a workflow they can use immediately.
options.pro: A specific judgement reveals the value of the product.
options.con: Requires source and alternate cuts that are cleared for use.

options.title: Show one source-linked export
options.pitch: Walk from an owned image to an exported copy with the source connection visible.
options.outcome: People see how the app makes creative work easier to trace.
options.pro: Demonstrates a concrete capability in a tight sequence.
options.con: The procedure may be less memorable than a good creative comparison.

options.title: Lead with a finished series
options.pitch: Open with a cohesive published series, then show the underlying workflow.
options.outcome: People encounter the calibre of the work before the software.
options.pro: Makes space for artwork with a real story.
options.con: The product benefit can disappear behind the gallery.

question: What should the next LoftwahFM release invite people to do?
context: Recent releases include a complete album and playable music videos. Different entry points reward different listening habits.
target: Recommend the invitation with the strongest listener payoff and an honest use of actual release artefacts. Treat plays and listener preference as unmeasured here.

options.title: Watch the performance cut
options.pitch: Lead with a strong moment from a published video and link straight to playback.
options.outcome: People can experience the song and the performance in one tap.
options.pro: Gives the release a specific moment to talk about.
options.con: The opening needs a quiet alternative for people browsing without sound.

options.title: Play the record from the start
options.pitch: Give the cover, first track and album sequence the lead.
options.outcome: People who listen in order reach the intended album experience.
options.pro: Preserves the arc of a complete release.
options.con: Requires a bigger time commitment from first-time listeners.

options.title: Turn on the station
options.pitch: Use a real radio programme or set to introduce the release in context.
options.outcome: People can discover the work as part of an ongoing listening session.
options.pro: Expresses LoftwahFM as a station with a point of view.
options.con: Makes the individual track or video less immediate.

question: Which work should get the next focused round?
context: The five priority surfaces need useful improvements and a higher creative bar. Choose work that can be evaluated against a visible result.
target: Rank options independently for current owner value and visible outcomes. Do not assume traffic analytics or a delivery effort that is not given.

options.title: Share discovery and Studio proof
options.pitch: Pick a small set of editable or usable work, build the discovery path and show its Studio source.
options.outcome: Visitors can find a relevant resource and understand where it came from.
options.pro: Addresses the reported discovery regression and the weak display choices.
options.con: Needs cross-project curation and actual usage checks.

options.title: Composer opening and campaigns
options.pitch: Take a selected art direction through a flagship landing view and one real social placement.
options.outcome: The public identity becomes tangible across two high-visibility surfaces.
options.pro: Lets the owner judge expression at the actual size of use.
options.con: Does little for the everyday resource search and signing flows.

options.title: Spin and Paperwork task openings
options.pitch: Prototype the most expressive usable first screen for a spin and for a clean PDF signing task.
options.outcome: Both tools become easier to recognise and use on a phone.
options.pro: Puts creative intensity and first-action performance in the same test.
options.con: Two separate apps need specific visual and workflow decisions.
